perspective:
Bradley Ochoa’s available information:

- He is a salesperson at a marketing firm and works with Katherine Lasiloo, the marketing manager and his colleague. Their professional relationship has involved some disagreement over traditional sales versus digital marketing.
- In the meeting room, he has prepared data/charts from the last five campaigns. He believes traditional sales techniques are being overlooked in favor of newer digital strategies. He says he appreciates Katherine’s digital work but thinks traditional methods help core sales; he is not suggesting abandoning digital, but feels proven methods are being sidelined. He hears Katherine say the market is evolving, digital outreach matters, and they should analyze data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shares recent digital campaign success stories that boosted engagement and sales. He asks how those strategies are developed. Katherine tells him it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offers to walk him through analytics and decision-making. He admits he had doubts about moving away from traditional methods but now wants to understand the digital approach. Katherine says she is glad he is open, that they must adapt and evolve, and suggests diving deeper.
- He proposes a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital strategies. Katherine agrees, says combining strengths could lead to better results, and suggests scheduling a brainstorm. He says he is hopeful and appreciates her willingness to collaborate. She says she looks forward to leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After a successful joint meeting, he is excited, works overtime, prepares a board presentation draft integrating both ideas, and shows it to Katherine. She reviews it, calls it comprehensive and well thought out, and says his hard work shows. He says he is convinced the integrated approach will set them apart from competitors and wants to nail the presentation. She says she is confident and suggests fine-tuning.
- After the presentation succeeds and the new strategy is implemented, he thanks Katherine, says he learned much from her and is grateful for his growth. She says it was a pleasure and that his openness made the partnership successful. He proposes regular strategy sessions. She agrees, saying they will keep on top of their game and market trends.

He does not have access to Katherine’s private thoughts, personality, education, or race unless she stated them or he observed them.
